items.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: I think there probably wouldn’t be a “Chicago jazz” had it not been for the New Orleans players going there. Because that’s what really turned on a lot of the players. ... until Earl Hines and Bix changed it again.

ctx.x: I’m glad you mentioned that because — is there a discernible difference between what happened to New Orleans jazz when it moved up to Chicago?

There sure is. The New Orleans players who kept playing it in Chicago influenced the people in Chicago. I think the Chicago tradition was largely a dance band — hotel bands, dance bands, ragtime players — and when King Oliver’s band went to Chicago, and before that Freddie Keppard with the Original Creole Band, they just showed a whole new way of playing. For instance I would doubt that there were a lot of bass players around Chicago who plucked the instrument. They probably bowed like every other bassist did,…
Don’t you kind of wish you could go back in time and witness some of that interaction?
